meta.title: Ch 2: General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 2 (General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities).

questions.q: An audit under SAs is designed to provide:
o: Absolute assurance that financial statements are correct in all respects
Reasonable assurance — a high but not complete level, subject to inherent limitations
A guarantee usable by investors as insurance
Assurance limited to detected frauds only
questions.why: SA 200: reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance obtained when sufficient appropriate evidence is obtained; absolute assurance is unattainable given sampling, judgment, and the inherent limitations (fraud concealment, persuasive not conclusive evidence).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the absolute-vs-reasonable contrast is the paper's first gate Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: Which of these is an INHERENT limitation on an audit's ability to detect misstatement?
o: Time pressure agreed with the client
Management concealing fraud through collusion and forged documents
The auditor not sampling enough items
Using outdated software
questions.why: Inherent limitations are built into the audit process: sampling, judgment, persuasive evidence, and fraud concealment (collusion, forgery) — they are excuses in principle; inadequate planning or staff is not, those are audit quality failures.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the list names limitations that are NOT excuses — staff cuts are failures, not limitations Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: No standard makes 'we were rushed' an inherent limitation.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: An auditor represents compliance with Standards on Auditing only if:
o: They followed the reporting SA carefully
They complied with ALL SAs relevant to the audit, not selected ones
Most major SAs were followed
The firm's internal manual was followed
questions.why: SA 200 is explicit: compliance with only some SAs does not represent compliance — and SAs do not override legal requirements; where law is more restrictive, both are complied with.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — one-of-many answers never represent compliance AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Compliance with all relevant SAs
mem.tip: Standards are a floor, and a floor covers the whole room.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: Professional scepticism in an audit most directly requires the auditor to:
o: Assume management is dishonest
Critically assess evidence and be alert to contradictions and reliability questions
Sign off faster where trust exists
Rely on prior-year comfort where controls are unchanged
questions.why: Scepticism = a questioning mind, alertness to evidence that contradicts or casts doubt, and reliability of documents/representations — it neither presumes dishonesty nor unquestioned trust.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the presumption trap on both sides is the whole question Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Trust nothing blindly — including last year's trust.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: Objectivity in the Code of Ethics requires the member to:
o: Never trust clients
Not subordinate judgment to others' feelings, prejudices, or conflict of interest
Sign everything management prepares
Avoid all non-audit services
questions.why: Objectivity = impartiality, integrity of judgment, freedom from conflicts that bias professional conclusions.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the phrase 'not subordinate to others' is the definition AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The judgment is yours before it is priced.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: Professional scepticism is best evidenced in the file by:
o: Ticking the same tests as last year
Documented challenge of contradictory evidence, testing of management explanations, and corroboration of important assertions
Refusing to speak to management
Reporting every query to the board
questions.why: Scepticism is procedural: contradiction chased, explanations corroborated, prior-year comfort re-tested where changed.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — file it or it didn't happen AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: The assertion that the entity HOLDS or CONTROLS rights to an asset is:
o: Existence
Rights and obligations
Valuation
Presentation
questions.why: Assertions: existence (there is an asset), rights/obligations (it's the client's), completeness (all are recorded), valuation/allocation, presentation/disclosure — leases and hypothecated stock live and die by the rights assertion.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — five assertions, tested in pairs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A booked asset may be the bank's; only one assertion finds that out.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: Who is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of financial statements?
o: The statutory auditor
Management (with oversight by those charged with governance)
ICAI
The audit firm's partner
questions.why: The division of responsibilities paragraph of every engagement letter: management prepares under the framework, TCWG oversee, the auditor opines — an auditor cannot audit the statements into existence by working on them.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — auditor = checker, never author AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: You can't referee your own goal and call it independence.
mem.link: Chapter 2 — General Auditing Principles and Auditors' Responsibilities

questions.q: 'Those charged with governance' in an audit context typically means:
o: The accounts team
The person(s) responsible for directing the entity and strategic obligations — board, audit committee
The shareholders' forum
Statutory auditors
questions.why: TCWG = the oversight layer (board/audit committee); the distinction matters for communications (independence, deficiencies, fraud), and for governance bodies that also manage, communication with those NOT charged with management is the safe channel.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — who watches the watchers Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: TCWG is the board's watch duty; management is its engine.
